name: From the house to the desk
summary: I drove the real camera on the frozen copy with a fake device and a fake speech recogniser, at 390 and 1024 px. On one probate estate I shot a sofa, a shotgun, a vase, a painting with six close-ups, a set of chairs, a box of books and the walkthrough's coin collection, then took them to the desk and pressed Name. The field side holds up well. The camera stays open, a spoken note lands on the right shot, a note said over a close-up goes to the item, the count and the maker said aloud reach qty and the name, a confirmed charity or auction house fills the recipient at capture, and a walkthrough collection goes onto its own line. The losses come after the shutter. The most serious one: the auction house the Job Plan auto-fills onto a line that turns out to be a firearm becomes its 'licensed dealer'. After a serial and two signatures the gate clears it to carry, and the release request tells the representatives they named that dealer on counsel's advice. Nobody named it. Second, once an item has more than four close-ups, the two agents read different ones. Agent Two never sees the first ones, which the guide tells the crew to take most important first. Third, what the crew says in the house is kept as words, not filled in for them. 'Going to Karen' is typed again at the desk, and until then the line is held off the request. Damage the crew names, like 'a big tear on the back', is kept out of the condition grade by the prompt. Vehicles arrive without the VIN, mileage and title the walkthrough already recorded, can never be photographed, and a car shot in the garage is counted twice with no duplicate flag. A firearm found in the house but not flagged at intake never lights the plan's banner for the next day's crew. Naming, the room check and the written release can only happen at the desk, after the crew has left, so a blurred hallmark or a missing back shot turns up when the object may already be gone. My proposals keep the rule that the field types nothing. The app would read the note against the people already on record, take a condition the crew says aloud as a person's grade, give vehicles a camera chip like collections, add a 'Check this room' pass before Lock, and let the representative sign the request on the iPad. Together these move most of the evening's retyping into presses the crew already makes, and the attorney would get a list where every value rests on the close-ups that were taken and no car or firearm is mis-recorded.
works_well: The camera never closes by itself and the shutter, chips, Close-up and Talk all survive the strip's repaint; overflow 0 at 390 and 1024 (fld3.js).
A spoken note is pinned to the shot it was started on and a note said after a close-up lands on the item (fld1: 'Moms, from Venice, going to Karen' on the vase, not on its close-up).

Agent One gets the crew's note, the room and the walkthrough's room note with every photograph; the maker said aloud goes into the name, the family's provenance is hedged ('Likely Venetian glass vase'), and the count said aloud goes to qty (fld1-agentIdentify.json, main-sync.gs:3409-3424).

The one confirmed charity or auction house fills the recipient at capture for Donate, Sell, Junk and Auction lines, marked 'from the Job Plan' (fld1: books -> Goodwill Palm Beach, sofa -> Kodner Galleries), apart from the firearm case in FLD-01.

Walkthrough collections show as a chip in the room and in the camera, and the shot goes onto the collection's own line under its number, with the latched chip dropped to Undecided so the walkthrough's instruction stands (fld1: 9700_col5 filled in place).
One Name press named all seven photographs, ran the room check and had Agent Two value them in the same run, with no further confirm (fld1 POSTS: agentIdentify, agentRoomCheck, agentValue x2).
Close-ups are captured sharper than other shots (1,200 px at 0.85) so marks stay legible, and the room's tiles flag '⚠ not saved' with Retry while the bytes are on the device.
measurements: Close-ups read per agent, painting with 6 close-ups through the real Close-up shutter (fld1.js -> fld1-agentIdentify.json, fld1-agentValue.json): Agent One got files up6, up7, up8, up9 (the first four); Agent Two got up11, up10, up9, up8 (the newest four). Close-ups 1-2 never reach the valuer and 5-6 never reach the namer.

Firearm under a latched Sell chip (fld2.js, fld2b.js): channel 'Kodner Galleries', channelFrom 'plan'; after typing serial RS12345M in the record and Record approval for both fiduciaries, invTransportBlocked = '' (cleared) and invTransportDealer = 'Kodner Galleries'. The request prints 'Serial RS12345M · to Kodner Galleries, a licensed dealer' and 'Every one goes to a licensed dealer, named by you on counsel's advice' (fld2-approval-request-before.html).

Vehicle brought in with Add → (fld2.js): the walkthrough held VIN WDDZF4JB1KA512345, 18,400 mi, title not located and a note; the line holds name, condition Good, serial undefined, room null, manual, no photo, and + Close-up is refused with 'Photograph the item in its room first'.

A car photographed in the garage plus the walkthrough vehicle (fld4.js): two lines (#1 with a photo, #2 manual), agentDuplicateGroups = [], no Possible duplicates on the tab; Agent Two valued #1 and 'Value 1 line' offers #2.

Firearm found but not flagged at intake (fld5.js): Job Plan .fa-banner absent, room workspace .fa-line absent, desk Urgent strip empty, while the inventory holds 'Remington 870 pump-action shotgun' in Firearms with a firearm notice.

Shot that failed on the iPad, seen on the laptop (fld6.js): the work bar reads 'Unnamed shots 4' beside 'Name 3 shots'; the row shows no state; the room's Retry says 'That photo can no longer be retried from this device — the image itself was not held. Re-shoot … if it is still on site.'

Presses between rooms on an estate (fld7.js, real controls, counting presses only): from one room's as-found camera to the next room's, 4 (Done, ← Rooms, room card, As found); one room's Next: Items + Done + as-found tick + Lock + back + next room + As found = 7, not counting shots. On a 15-room house that is about 165 presses that are not photographs.

Camera strip on a phone (fld3.js at 390x844): the controls start at y=489 and fill 355 px; after one item and 5 close-ups it reads 'Last: detail of the item before it · shot 5' and '6 shots' (close-ups counted as shots). No item name, no close-up count, no hint that only four are read.
Room tiles (fld3.js, 390 and 1024): the only control on an Items tile is 'Delete this photo'; reopening the camera leaves Close-up disabled until a new item is shot (fld1 CONTROLS).
verifier_note: The report holds up well. I reran its claims with two scripts of my own on the frozen copy. Where it mattered I used the real controls: the Job Plan's vendor and status selects, the camera's chips, shutter, Close-up and Talk, the row's ▾, the record's serial box, the row's pick box, the bulk bar's Record approval and the dialog's ticks. Every behaviour I could drive came out as reported. Three of the auditor's pieces of evidence were weak. (1) In fld1, the 'Good' grade on the sofa came from the auditor's own stub, so it proves nothing about FLD-04; that finding rests on the prompt text alone and stays PLAUSIBLE. (2) fld4 called agentDuplicateGroups with J undefined: the job id sits outside the evaluate call, so the [] it printed was meaningless. My v2 made the correct call and still got []. (3) In fld2, the firearm defect depended on vendorSourcing seeded directly; I reproduced it through the real selects. FLD-10's inconsistency is real, but its proposal goes against Anthony's Q40 answer ('Next: Items in the camera … on every job'). I lowered four severities: FLD-03, FLD-08 and FLD-14 to medium, FLD-12 kept at medium, FLD-10 to low.

findings.title: The Job Plan's auction house (or charity, or hauler) becomes a firearm's 'licensed dealer' on the PR's written transport authority
findings.where: Field camera chip latched → _captureShot calls invFillPlanChannel (havellin.html:40688); invFillPlanChannel (39581) has no firearm exclusion; invTransportDealer (30034) reads any channel off Distribute; invTransportBlocked (30006); printApprovalRequest's Firearms: written authority block. The same fill runs from _invEdit / _invBulkApply when a disposition is set at the desk, and from invFillPlanChannels when a vendor is confirmed later.
findings.evidence: fld2.js / fld2b.js: Sell latched, then the shotgun is shot; Agent One files it as Firearms; the line holds channel 'Kodner Galleries' with channelFrom 'plan' (the record shows 'from the Job Plan'). After the serial is typed in the record and both fiduciaries are ticked in Record approval, invTransportBlocked returns '' and invTransportDealer returns 'Kodner Galleries'. fld2-approval-request-before.html prints 'Serial RS12345M · to Kodner Galleries, a licensed dealer' and 'Every one goes to a licensed dealer, named by you on counsel's advice … Licensed dealer: Kodner Galleries'. The code's own warning at havellin.html:28020 says the dealer arm 'is satisfied by any non-empty channel'. Donate or Remove latched gives Goodwill or the junk hauler the same role (same function, by code).
findings.tc_impact: A firearm shot while the previous pile's chip is still latched (the normal rhythm) arrives as Sell to the auction house. The TC sees a small grey 'from the Job Plan' and moves on. The representatives sign a written authority naming a party nobody chose, and the gate tells Anthony he is cleared to carry. A trust attorney reads 'named by you on counsel's advice', which is false.
findings.proposal: invFillPlanChannel returns false for invIsFirearm(ref). When a line becomes Firearms (_agWrite, _invEdit, _invBulkApply), a channel marked channelFrom 'plan' is cleared and the latched field disposition goes back to '' (a firearm's destination is the protocol's and the representatives'). invTransportDealer ignores any channel still marked 'plan', because a dealer is only ever named by a person. The row then reads 'no dealer named' in bronze, and the request lists the firearm under 'not covered for transport' until someone types the dealer.
findings.vnote: Reproduced independently, through real controls only. On the Job Plan's own selects I chose Kodner Galleries for the estimate's auction line and set it Confirmed. In the Garage I latched Sell on the camera and shot a photograph that Agent One named 'Remington 870 pump-action shotgun' and filed as Firearms. The line came to the desk with disposition Sell, channel 'Kodner Galleries' and channelFrom 'plan'. invTransportDealer returned 'Kodner Galleries' at once. I typed serial RS12345M in the record's own box, picked the row, pressed the bulk bar's Record approval, ticked both fiduciaries and saved. invTransportBlocked then returned '' and the record read '✓ Cleared to carry. Havellin’s named principal alone takes it to Kodner Galleries, in a locked case.' Before the approval, the request printed 'Serial RS12345M · to Kodner Galleries, a licensed dealer', followed by 'Every one goes to a licensed dealer, named by you on counsel’s advice … Licensed dealer: Kodner Galleries'. In the code: invFillPlanChannel (havellin.html:39581) has no firearm exclusion and is called at capture (40688), from _invEdit (29781) and _invBulkApply (37372) on a disposition change, and from invFillPlanChannels (39600). invTransportDealer (30034) reads any channel off Distribute, and nothing clears channelFrom when a line becomes Firearms; only typing a channel does (29779, 37371). Donate and Junk would hand a charity or a hauler the same dealer role through the same function (from the code; not driven). The written firearms transport authority names a party nobody chose as the licensed dealer, and the gate clears it.

findings.title: With more than four close-ups, Agent Two never sees the first ones, which the guide says to take most important first
findings.where: invLineCloseUps (havellin.html:40794) sorts newest first, slice(0, AGENT_MAX_DETAILS=4); _agDetailRefs (37570) sorts oldest first. The camera strip (_fieldCamPaint) has no count or limit. photography-guide.html:481 says 'Most important first: the app only reads the first four.'
findings.evidence: fld1.js: six close-ups of the painting through the real Close-up shutter. fld1-agentIdentify.json: Agent One details up6–up9. fld1-agentValue.json (research mode): Agent Two details up11, up10, up9, up8. fld3.js: after five close-ups the strip says only 'Last: detail of the item before it · shot 5' and '6 shots'.
findings.tc_impact: The line with the best evidence (a signed painting, a hallmark) is researched without the signature the crew shot first, and nothing on screen says so. The attorney gets a comparables figure whose basis never read the mark. The crew is never told that a fifth or sixth close-up is wasted.
findings.proposal: One ordering for both agents: close-ups added at the desk first (invAddCloseUp stamps addedOn:'desk'), then the field's close-ups in the order taken. Raise the research cap to 6 for Agent Two. The camera strip names the item and counts its close-ups ('Close-ups of the sofa: 4 · the agents read four'), and says so once the fourth is taken. Correct the guide's sentence for both agents.
findings.vnote: I took six close-ups of a painting with the real Close-up shutter; their files are up4 to up9 in the order taken. Agent One's request carried up4 to up7 (the first four). Agent Two's research request carried up9, up8, up7 and up6 (the newest four), so up4 and up5, the first two, never reach the valuer. photography-guide.html:480-481 tells the crew 'Most important first: the app only reads the first four.' After six close-ups the camera strip read only 'Last: detail of the item before it · shot 6' with a count of '9 shots': no close-up count and no limit shown. The newest-first order for Agent Two was a deliberate 2026-10-26 choice, so that a close-up added at the desk gets read (the comment at havellin.html:40789-40793). The finding is that this order collides with the guide's promise once a line has more than four close-ups. It is not in Known, not fixed, and the proposal (desk close-ups first, then the field's in the order taken) honours both intents.
findings.vrepro: FLD-verify/v1.out: 'painting close-ups in the order taken: [up4,up5,up6,up7,up8,up9]'; 'AGENT ONE painting details: [up4,up5,up6,up7]'; 'AGENT TWO … mode comps details [up9,up8,up7,up6]'; bodies in FLD-verify/v1-agentIdentify.json and v1-agentValue.json. Code: havellin.html:40794-40803 (invLineCloseUps sorts by b.ts - a.ts) and 37570-37574 (_agDetailRefs sorts by a.ts - b.ts).

findings.title: Who gets it, said aloud in the house, is typed again for every line at the desk, and the line is held off the request until it is
findings.where: Agent One's notes rule (apps-script/main-sync.gs:3419-3424: who it is going to 'never goes in the name') and _avLineText (main-sync.gs:4513). No reader writes the channel from the field note. The desk's box is _invRecipientInput / _invBenListAttr (havellin.html ~39600). Lines with nobody named are held off the request (invReleaseRecipientNamed).
findings.evidence: fld1.js: vase shot under To a person with Talk 'Moms, from Venice, going to Karen'; job.beneficiaries holds Karen Price; after Name and Agent Two the line is Distribute with channel '' (fld1.out LINE 4). fld2.js: golf clubs with 'Going to Thomas' (Thomas Price on the roster), channel ''. The Evening Desk guide: 'Items with nobody in Who takes it wait off it.' Disputes ('both kids want it') and promises in the will said at the camera are likewise only words in the note.
findings.tc_impact: For each To-a-person line the TC reads the note, clicks the box, types and picks the name: three or four actions plus typing on the lines an estate cares about most. Until that is done the line cannot go on the release request.
findings.proposal: A DOM-free invNoteRecipient(job, ref) matches the field note against jobFiduciaries, job.beneficiaries and, on living work, the intake's family names (first or full name). On a live Distribute line with no channel, never a firearm, it pre-fills the channel with channelFrom:'note' and shows 'from the field note' under the box, the same pattern as 'from the Job Plan'. Typing over it clears the mark, and the row's one Reviewed tick confirms it. For a name on no roster, Agent One returns an optional saidTo string (never a disposition), offered in the record as one tap: 'Use Karen (said in the house)'. Likewise saidDisputed offers the disputed flag and saidBequest offers the bequest flag.
findings.decided_conflict: Decided: 'Agent One writing a value, a disposition or an NFA flag'. This writes no disposition: the recipient is a suggestion marked as coming from the note. The rule 'the field types nothing' is unchanged.
findings.vnote: I shot a vase under To a person and said 'This was mom's, going to Karen'; Karen Price is on job.beneficiaries. After naming and valuing, the line read disposition Distribute with channel ''. printApprovalRequest held it off the request ('held': the vase), and no code writes channel from fieldNote (grep). The comment at havellin.html:40590 says by design that the recipient 'is named at the desk off the voice note'. A pre-fill marked 'from the field note' and confirmed at the desk keeps that rule and 'the field types nothing'. It is a suggestion, not a disposition, so it does not touch the Decided item on Agent One writing a disposition. I rated it medium rather than high: the desk box already offers the roster (_invBenListAttr), so typing a name costs a few keystrokes per line, and holding an unnamed line off the request is correct behaviour.
findings.vrepro: FLD-verify/v1.out: 'VASE: {disp:Distribute, ch:"", note:"This was mom's, going to Karen"}'; 'REQUEST (before serial): held:["Likely Venetian glass vase, blue and gold"]'. Prompt: apps-script/main-sync.gs:3419-3424 (who it is going to never goes in the name).

findings.title: Damage the crew names ('big tear on the back', 'one has a broken leg') is kept out of the condition grade, so the papers say Good
findings.where: AGENT_CONDITION_TEXT (apps-script/main-sync.gs:3261: 'Grade only what the photograph shows of the thing itself'). Agent One's notes section (3419) takes only the count, maker and size from the note. Agent Two's condition rule (~4380) treats only a desk-set grade as a person's (conditionChecked). _invAgentCondition writes condBy 'agent'.
findings.evidence: fld1.js: sofa with Talk 'Crate and Barrel, the back cushion has a big tear and a pet stain'. fld1-agentValue.json: the line goes to Agent Two with condition 'Good', conditionChecked false, and the tear only inside fieldNote. The prompts tell both agents to grade from the photograph alone. This is reasoning from the prompt text; the stubbed agents cannot show what the live model would grade.
findings.tc_impact: The Contents Record, the Court Inventory and the value treat a torn sofa or a damaged set of chairs as undamaged unless the TC catches each note and sets the condition by hand. A trust officer sees a figure for property in better shape than it is.
findings.proposal: Treat the crew's words as a person's account. Agent One's CONDITION section and AGENT_CONDITION_TEXT gain one sentence: 'damage the crew names in their note counts as seen: grade it so'. A grade backed by the note is recorded as condBy 'field' and sent to Agent Two as conditionChecked ('value it in this condition'). The record reads 'Poor · said in the house: "big tear and a pet stain"'.
findings.vnote: The auditor's evidence is circular: in fld1 the 'Good' grade came from its own Agent One stub. What I can confirm: Agent One receives the note ('The back cushion has a big tear and a pet stain on the back'), and Agent Two receives it as fieldNote, with conditionChecked false. AGENT_CONDITION_TEXT (main-sync.gs:3261-3264) says 'Grade only what the photograph shows of the thing itself'. Agent One's notes section (3419-3424) lists only the count, maker and size as what to take from a note. So on a literal reading, damage the crew names but the photograph does not show stays out of the grade. Agent Two is told to 'adjust for any condition that is recorded' (4375), so the figure may allow for the tear while the grade printed on the papers says otherwise. Condition is not one of the row's columns, so the reviewer sees the 🎤 note but not the grade unless they open the record. I cannot test how the live model actually grades here.
findings.vrepro: apps-script/main-sync.gs:3261-3264, 3419-3424, 3483-3484, 4375-4386; FLD-verify/v1.out 'AGENT ONE sofa fieldNote: The back cushion has a big tear…' and 'AGENT TWO soq-10 … cond "" false | note The back cushion has a big tear…'.

findings.title: Vehicles lose the VIN, mileage and title the walkthrough recorded, and can never be photographed
findings.where: materializeVehicle (havellin.html:36189) copies only the name, condition and collector flag. The walkthrough form records vin, mileage, titleLocated and a note (57107-57165). invCloseUpRefusal (40755) refuses manual lines. photography-guide.html:602-604: 'Cars and boats: No item photo … Keep them out of the garage's photos.'
findings.evidence: fld2.js: walkthrough vehicle with VIN WDDZF4JB1KA512345, 18,400 mi, title not located, note 'Title not found; spare key in kitchen drawer'. After Add → the line holds name '2019 Mercedes-Benz E350 sedan', condition Good, serial undefined, room null, manual, no photo. + Close-up is refused with 'This line has no photograph yet. Photograph the item in its room first' — the opposite of what the guide says.
findings.tc_impact: The TC copies the VIN from the estimate into Serial Number by hand, and the mileage and title have nowhere to go. The car reaches the Court Inventory with no photograph and no VIN. Agent Two (on Value N lines) has no mileage to work from.
findings.proposal: Vehicles join the inventory by themselves, as collections do (the collectionLinesEnsure pattern), so the Add → press goes. The line carries vin→serial, the mileage into the name ('… 18,400 mi'), and the title as a flag on the record. A vehicle chip in the camera, like the collection chip, takes the photo onto the vehicle's line, with Close-up for the VIN plate and the odometer. The guide's Cars row becomes 'tap its chip and photograph it'.
findings.vnote: I pressed the walkthrough panel's real 'Add →' for a vehicle recorded with VIN WDDZF4JB1KA512345, 18,400 miles, title not located and a note. The line holds the name '2019 Mercedes-Benz E350 sedan' and condition Good; serial is undefined, room null, manual true, no photograph. The VIN, the mileage, the title flag and the note go nowhere (materializeVehicle, havellin.html:36189-36205). + Close-up is not offered in the vehicle's record; invCloseUpRefusal says 'Photograph the item in its room first'. photography-guide.html:602-604 says 'No item photo … Keep them out of the garage's photos', so the two contradict each other. The proposal follows the P24 collections pattern. 'Vehicles are still brought in by hand' in CLAUDE.md describes current behaviour, not a decision, and nothing on the Decided list is touched.

findings.title: A car photographed in the garage and the walkthrough's vehicle are two lines, and nothing flags it
findings.where: materializeVehicle / _importedSourceSet (checks sourceVehId only). agentDuplicateGroups / _agDupEligible (lines Agent One named only). The room check reads only photographed lines in a room. Collections have collectionUseLine; vehicles have nothing like it.
findings.evidence: fld4.js: one Items photo in the Garage named 'Mercedes-Benz E-Class sedan, silver' (Vehicles & Watercraft) plus the walkthrough vehicle added → two lines (#1 photo, #2 manual). agentDuplicateGroups = [], no Possible duplicates on the tab. Agent Two valued #1, and the work bar offers 'Value 1 line' for #2.
findings.tc_impact: The inventory, the Court Inventory and a Form 706 figure carry the car twice unless the TC happens to notice. The guide's only defence is 'keep them out of the garage's photos'.
findings.proposal: When Agent One files a photographed line as Vehicles & Watercraft on a job whose walkthrough has a vehicle, the desk offers 'Use that line', exactly as for a collection (the collectionUseLine pattern): the vehicle's line takes the photograph and keeps its number and VIN. agentDuplicateGroups also joins a sourceVehId line with any Vehicles & Watercraft line that shares its make or model words. With FLD-05's chip the photo lands on the vehicle's line in the first place.
findings.vnote: A Garage Items photograph named 'Mercedes-Benz E-Class sedan, silver' (Vehicles & Watercraft), plus the walkthrough vehicle brought in through 'Add →', gives two lines: #1 with a photograph in room 5 and #5 with no photograph and no room. I called agentDuplicateGroups(9820) properly (the auditor's fld4 passed an undefined job id, so its [] proved nothing) and still got []; the tab shows no Possible duplicates. In the code, _agDupEligible needs namedBy agent and a room, and the room check reads only photographed lines, so a sourceVehId line can never be joined. Only the guide's instruction to keep cars out of the photographs stands against a car counted twice on the Court Inventory or the 706.
findings.vrepro: FLD-verify/v2.out: 'LINES: 1 | Mercedes-Benz E-Class sedan, silver | Vehicles & Watercraft | 5 | photo … 5 | 2019 Mercedes-Benz E350 sedan | Vehicles & Watercraft |  | no photo'; 'DUP GROUPS: []'; 'Possible duplicates on tab: false'. Code: havellin.html:37954-37957, 38006-38070.

findings.title: A firearm found in the house but not flagged at intake never warns the crew afterwards
findings.where: firearmsBannerHtml (havellin.html:10991) and firearmsWorkspaceLine (11003) read only firearmsFlaggedAtIntake. The desk's Urgent strip (deskAlertsHtml, 48073) uses the same line.
findings.evidence: fld5.js: shotgun photographed in the Garage, named Firearms with a firearm notice; intake flag false. On the Job Plan .fa-banner is absent, the Kitchen workspace's .fa-line is absent, and the desk's Urgent strip is empty.
findings.tc_impact: The next day's crew works the house with no 'firearms in this house: photograph in place, nothing moves' line. The protocol's first rule rests on whoever happened to read the desk's notice list.
findings.proposal: One predicate, jobHasFirearms(job): the intake flag, or any live line where invIsFirearm holds, or an Agent One firearm or NFA notice. The banner and the room line read it ('Firearm found on site: #2 Remington 870, Garage. Nothing moves'), and a firearm found without the intake flag sits in the Urgent strip until the line is reviewed.
findings.vnote: Intake firearms flag false. After a shotgun was named Firearms with a firearm notice, the Job Plan had no .fa-banner, the Kitchen workspace had no .fa-line, and the desk's Urgent strip (#desk-alerts) was empty. firearmsBannerHtml and firearmsWorkspaceLine (havellin.html:10991-11008) read only firearmsFlaggedAtIntake; deskAlertsHtml uses the same line (48087). The desk does still show the row's '⚠ held' and Agent One's Firearm notice, but nothing on the crew's screens says so.
findings.vrepro: FLD-verify/v1.out: 'intake firearms flag: false', 'desk Urgent strip: ""', 'Job Plan .fa-banner present: false', 'Kitchen workspace .fa-line present: false' (all after the shotgun was named Firearms).

findings.title: Naming and the room check run only at the desk, so a blurred mark or a missing close-up is found after the crew has left
findings.where: agentNameShots is called only from the desk's work bar (havellin.html:39375). The room workspace (_paintRoomWorkspace) has no naming or check. + Close-up after the fact (invAddCloseUp) needs the object in front of you. Agent One's 'other' notice is for 'a mark or label that is there but too small or blurred to read' (main-sync.gs:3477).
findings.evidence: grep: agentNameShots( is called only at 39375. The room tiles read 'Item N · undecided' until the evening run (fld3.js). AGENT_BATCH 20 with AGENT_PARALLEL 8 means a 20-photo room is a single call; the 2026-10-26 probe named one photograph in 10 s. The timing for a whole room is reasoning, not measured.
findings.tc_impact: The evening finds the 'Look at this' notices, the painting with no back shot, the low-confidence names and the doubles. Fixing any of them needs the object, which may have gone with the vendor, or needs a second visit.
findings.proposal: '✓ Check this room' in the room workspace, above Lock: it sends the room's unnamed Items shots to Agent One, then the room check, and lists what to do while still in the room. That covers Agent One's 'other' notices (mark unreadable: take a close-up), lines in an intrinsic category with no close-up (the guide's own table: 'Oil painting: the signature and the back; say the size'), low-confidence names, and possible doubles. Each has a one-tap camera armed on that line (FLD-09). The evening's Name shots then finds the room already named.
findings.vnote: The description is accurate. agentNameShots is defined at havellin.html:37736, and its only call site is the desk's work bar (39375); the room workspace (_paintRoomWorkspace, 41535) offers no naming or check, and room tiles read 'Item N · Sell' until the evening run. The proposal conflicts with nothing on the Decided list: it is optional and keeps 'the field types nothing'. I lowered it to medium for three reasons. On an estate nothing leaves before written approval, so the object is usually still in the house the next day. + Close-up after the fact already exists. A field pass needs signal in the house, which FLD-11 shows is not certain. The minutes a room would take are reasoning, not measured.

findings.title: In the room, a shot can only be deleted: no changing where it goes, no ⚑, no close-up after the camera closes
findings.where: _roomShotStripHtml (havellin.html:41483): a tile carries the bin and Retry only. openFieldCamera sets last:null, so Close-up is disabled on reopening.
findings.evidence: fld3.js at 390 and 1024: the tile's buttons are ['Delete this photo', …]. fld1 CONTROLS at camera open: 'Close-up … (disabled)'.
findings.tc_impact: A chip left latched from the last pile (the commonest field slip), a forgotten ⚑ or a missed hallmark can only be fixed at the desk, in the evening, away from the object.
findings.proposal: Each Items tile gets three small controls: where it goes (the field chips as a select, written through _invEdit), ⚑, and Close-up, which opens the camera armed on that item (openFieldCamera(…, {closeUpOf: stableId}) sets last to that line).
findings.vnote: The room's Items tiles carry only 'Delete this photo' (Retry or Mark lost appear only on a shot that failed). openFieldCamera resets last:null (havellin.html:40887), so Close-up stays disabled when the camera is reopened. In field mode the desk, and with it + Close-up, is hidden (a Known item, in the sign-out context), so a missed close-up or a wrong latched chip can only be fixed out of field mode.
findings.vrepro: FLD-verify/v1.out 'ROOM TILES: ["Delete this photo :: …Item 1 · Sell", …]'; havellin.html:41483-41532 (_roomShotStripHtml), 40887.

findings.title: On an estate the as-found camera says 'Next: Items' although the guide says the whole house goes first; walking the passes costs about 11 presses a room
findings.where: _fieldCamPaint (havellin.html:41032) shows Next: Items in 'before' mode on every job; fieldCamNextItems (41114). photography-guide.html:436: 'On an estate, take the as-found photos of the whole house before anyone sorts anything.'
findings.evidence: fld7.js on a probate job: the as-found camera offers only ['Next: Items →']. From one room's as-found camera to the next room's takes 4 presses (Done, ← Rooms, room card, As found). One room's Items, as-found tick, Lock and the move to the next room take 7, not counting shots.
findings.tc_impact: The one button on screen sends the crew to sort a room before the rest of the house is recorded as found, which is the order the guide forbids on an estate. On a 15-room house the walk between rooms is about 165 presses that are not photographs.
findings.proposal: On a decedent job the as-found camera's button reads 'Next room: As found →' (the next room with no as-found shot) and ticks As-found pass complete for the room it leaves, if the person confirms. After the last room it offers 'Start Items in <first room>'. The Items camera ends with 'Lock & next room →'. Living jobs keep Next: Items.
findings.vnote: The inconsistency is real. On a probate job, the as-found camera offers only 'Next: Items →' (my v2 run), while photography-guide.html:436 says that on an estate the whole house is photographed as found before anyone sorts. The proposal, though, replaces Next: Items on decedent jobs. Anthony's Q40 answer (2026-10-09, WORKFLOW_AUDIT:1031) was '*Next: Items* in the camera and *Cleared* on the room's row on every job; estates keep the tick and the refusal', recorded in CLAUDE.md's Domain rules ('The as-found pass ends with **Next: Items** … P25, Q40'). A fix that leaves Q40 alone would add a 'Next room: As found' beside Next: Items on estates, or reword the guide. The press counts are the auditor's (fld7) and plausible; I did not recount them.
findings.vrepro: FLD-verify/v2.out: 'as-found camera next buttons: ["Next: Items →"]' on job 9820 (probate). havellin.html:41030-41032; photography-guide.html:436-440; WORKFLOW_AUDIT_2026-09-28.md:1029-1031.

findings.title: A shot still held on the iPad looks lost on the laptop, and Retry there says to re-shoot it
findings.where: retryPhotoUpload (havellin.html:41765) alert; _renderInvRow shows no upload state; the work bar's Unnamed chip counts it.
findings.evidence: fld6.js: a shot that failed in the house (its bytes on the iPad), with the note 'Signed Tiffany lamp, going to Karen', seen on the laptop. The work bar reads 'Unnamed shots 4' beside 'Name 3 shots'. The row shows no state and no photo. The room's Retry alerts 'That photo can no longer be retried from this device — the image itself was not held. Re-shoot HVL_9700_INV_2.jpg if it is still on site.'
findings.tc_impact: At night the TC sees a count that does not add up, a line with a note and no picture, and an instruction to go back and re-shoot, when the photo is sitting on Ashley's iPad waiting for signal.
findings.proposal: Record who captured the shot on the line (heldBy: deviceUser()). On a device without the bytes, the row, the tile and Retry say '⚠ Not in Drive yet: held on Ashley Jerome's device. Open the app there with signal.' The work bar counts 'N waiting for upload' separately from Unnamed shots.
findings.vnote: The fixture is reachable. The manifest carries status (havellin.html:27562), and the laptop's own _expireStaleUploads turns an upload still running on the iPad into 'failed' after the timeout (27390); failed uploads never retry by themselves. On the laptop, the Kitchen tile read '⚠ not saved Retry'. Pressing Retry alerted 'That photo can no longer be retried from this device — the image itself was not held. Re-shoot HVL_9820_INV_2.jpg if it is still on site.' The desk row showed no state. The work bar read 'Unnamed shots 4' while naming sent 3 shots, and 'Unnamed shots 1' after the run. A related case I found: for an as-found shot that failed on the other device, this laptop offers 'Mark lost' (shotMarkLostOffered tests only this device's _photoRetryData). One press would record as lost an as-found shot whose bytes may still be on the iPad. I did not drive what that does on the iPad, so that part is reasoning.
findings.vrepro: FLD-verify/v2.out: 'Kitchen tiles: ["…As found 1⚠ not saved, image not held Mark lost", "…Item 3 · undecided“Signed Tiffany lamp, going to Karen”⚠ not saved Retry"]'; 'Retry says: [alert: That photo can no longer be retried from this device …Re-shoot HVL_9820_INV_2.jpg if it is still on site.]'; 'identify sent: [[s0,s1,s3]]'. Code: havellin.html:41765-41775, shotMarkLostOffered.

findings.title: With two selling vendors (or charities) confirmed, every Sell line says 'name one', though the crew sorted the piles separately
findings.where: invPlanChannel / invFillPlanChannel (havellin.html:39565-39593) fill nothing when several vendors are confirmed; the row's warning '_pcRow.many' (39643); FIELD_DISPOSITIONS has one Sell chip.
findings.evidence: From the code: with an auction house and an estate sale company both Confirmed, invPlanChannel returns {many} and every Sell row carries '2 confirmed: name one'. The camera chip latches per pile, so in the house the crew already knows which pile is the auction's and which the estate sale's.
findings.tc_impact: One recipient typed per selling line, or a filter and a bulk-bar sweep per vendor, for a split the crew had already made in the house.
findings.proposal: Where two or more vendors of a kind are Confirmed, the camera's Sell (or Donate) chip splits into one chip per vendor ('Sell · Kodner', 'Sell · estate sale'), each latching with its pile, and the shot takes that vendor with channelFrom 'plan'. Never on a firearm (FLD-01).
findings.vnote: I confirmed Kodner Galleries and an estate sale company through the Job Plan's selects, then set a line to Sell with its row's own select. The channel stayed empty and the row read '2 confirmed: name one' (invPlanChannel returns {many}; havellin.html:39565-39579, 39644). The proposal (one chip per confirmed vendor, chosen by the crew) is not a guess, so it keeps Q44's 'never guessed'. It does widen the seven-chip FIELD_DISPOSITIONS catalogue the Domain rules describe, which Anthony should see. That the crew knows in the house which pile goes to which vendor is the auditor's judgement, not something I observed.

findings.title: The representative standing in the house cannot give the written release on the iPad
findings.where: The P28 pad (signPadInit, signPadSigned) is used only by the agreement dialog (havellin.html:23318) and the sign-out dialog (31849). The release request goes only by Send request, print, scan and Record the signed request (invRecordRequestApproval 33187, invSaveApproval 33218).
findings.evidence: grep of signPadSigned/signPadDataUrl callers; the Evening Desk guide's round (Send request → Gmail → I've sent it → signed copy back → Record the signed request → File signed copy). Sign-out of an estate line waits on invApprovalComplete.
findings.tc_impact: The executor and co-representative who decide in the house what goes where cannot approve it there. The round trip takes a day or more plus about eight presses at night, and nothing on an estate leaves (vendor pickups, family hand-overs) until it is done, which often means another visit.
findings.proposal: '✍️ Sign on the iPad' on the approval request card, also reachable from the Job Plan in field mode. It shows the request (the same printApprovalRequest page) with an initial pad per group and a signature pad for each fiduciary present. Done files the PDF through fileSignedCopy (kind approval) and records the signers through invApprovalWithSigners. A co-representative who is absent signs later (a partial approval, as today). It sits beside the DocuSign route planned in Open work.
findings.decided_conflict: Domain rule 'Verbal approval is never accepted': a signature on the glass is written approval, as the P28/P29 routes already treat it.
findings.vnote: The P28 pad is used only by the agreement dialog (signPadSigned and signPadDataUrl at havellin.html:23318-23323) and the sign-out dialog (31769, 31849-31854). The release request goes only by Send request, print or scan, then Record the signed request or Record approval. A signature on the glass is written approval, so 'Verbal approval is never accepted' is not touched. Not a duplicate: Open work's next build is a DocuSign route for the request ('definitely docusign'), which this would sit beside. I lowered it to medium: an estate's fiduciaries are often not in the house, and the request letter shipped on 2026-10-26.

findings.title: New-home lines on a Home Transition carry no room at the new home
findings.where: FIELD_DISPOSITIONS 'move' (havellin.html:40594) and _invRecipient (Move derives the destination address only); the Job Plan's nh_floorplan task (45650) and the move-day procedure ('placed by the approved floor plan').
findings.evidence: grep: there is no destination-room field anywhere; a Move line's 'Where it goes' is the address.
findings.tc_impact: The crew knows in the room that the sofa goes to the new living room, but the placement plan for the movers is kept outside the inventory, and the Contents Record cannot say where things went.
findings.proposal: On a Home Transition, when New home is latched, a second chip row lists the new home's rooms (typed once on the floor-plan task) and latches with it. The line records destRoom, and the Contents Record and a movers' list print it by room.
findings.vnote: There is no destination-room field anywhere: grep for destRoom or a room at the new home finds nothing. The floor-plan task (nh_floorplan, havellin.html:45650) and the move-day procedure ('direct the movers by the approved floor plan', 45747) keep the placement plan off the inventory. The proposal conflicts with no decided rule. It adds a second chip row in the field, which is a cost to weigh against 'thorough, never cumbersome'.
